transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Everwell Head of Cloud Ops), Dr. Omar Rahman (ML Lead), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary: Quick POC scoping to finalize network setup (VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Interface endpoints), confirm data residency, define success criteria and run benchmarks and timelines for a 2-week pilot. Some audio / auto-transcription artifacts present.

Topics: private networking options, regions, egress constraints, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, success criteria, security/compliance paperwork.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Samir is our SE.
[00:08] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here. I'll own the benchmark and network setup for the POC.
[00:12] Lena (Everwell): Hi, Lena. Thanks for coordinating. We have Dr. Omar and Priya on as well.
[00:17] Omar (Everwell ML): Morning, thanks.
[00:19] Priya (Everwell Sec): Hello.
[00:22] Maya: Goal for today is to agree on the private networking approach (VPC peering vs PrivateLink/Interface endpoints), regions and any egress constraints, plus define success criteria and pilot timeline.
[00:30] Lena: Yes, our compliance team wants all inference traffic to stay within our AWS accounts and not traverse public internet. We also need logs and auditability.
[00:38] Priya: To add, we have a hard egress policy in our west region — no outbound internet from the inference subnet. So PrivateLink or VPC peering is required, or some managed NAT excluded.
[00:49] Samir: Got it. For Redwood private deployments we typically support either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. Peering is straightforward if you're okay with route table changes; PrivateLink gives a more managed interface and avoids touching route tables across accounts. There are tradeoffs on cross-AZ latencies.
[01:05] Omar: Latency is important. Our target is sub-120ms p95 for single-request text generation at 512 tokens, and throughput roughly 30 qps sustained for the pilot. Does that seem reasonable?
[01:16] Samir: 30 QPS at 512 tokens is in scope; we'll want to define concurrency and batching in the benchmark. For p95 under 120ms we need to choose the right instance and ensure the private network path doesn't add more than ~20-30ms.
[01:28] Maya: We should capture the success criteria now: 1) p95 latency <= 120ms for 512-token generation under defined load, 2) sustained throughput 30 QPS, 3) data never leaves specified AWS region, 4) audits and access logs delivered to Everwell, and 5) pass a simple quality check on outputs. Agree?
[01:44] Priya: Yes, and add that encryption in transit must use TLS with mutual auth to your side for PrivateLink. Also want SOC2 docs.
[01:51] Maya: We'll include TLS mutual auth notes and SOC2 pack.
[01:54] Lena: On region preferences, primary region is us-west-2, backup us-east-1. We prefer to keep the pilot in us-west-2.
[02:02] Samir: Cool. For VPC peering we need your VPC CIDR and the subnet ranges to allocate for the inference endpoints. For PrivateLink we publish an endpoint service and you create interface endpoints in your account. Small note: if you have strict egress blocking we need to ensure the interface endpoints are allowed in the subnet's security group and NACLs.
[02:20] Priya: We will verify allowed security groups. We also have an internal requirement that any cross-account IAM role used must be auditable.
[02:27] Maya: Noted. We'll provide a network runbook with exact steps for both approaches and the minimum IAM/SG/NACL changes.
[02:33] Omar: For workload sizing, our model is a 7B encoder-decoder with 512 token context. Typical prompt size is 80 tokens, outputs around 150 tokens. So effective sequence about 230 tokens average but worst-case 512. We'll send model config.
[02:45] Samir: That helps. For benching we'll test two profiles: typical load (230 tokens avg) and worst-case (512). We'll simulate 30 qps sustained with bursts to 60 for 30s. We'll also test cold-start and warm KV cache scenarios.
[02:59] Lena: On data residency: we store PHI in upstream systems; inference inputs may include hashed PHI. We need to ensure Redwood does not persist raw inputs and that logs are retained in our S3 bucket or sent via syslog.
[03:12] Priya: Also need the ability to disable any optional telemetry.
[03:16] Maya: We have a PII/data handling doc and an option to disable logging of payloads; audit logs can be forwarded to your S3 or to CloudWatch via a cross-account role. We'll include that in the security pack.
[03:28] Samir: On benchmarking metrics we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and network egress per hour. We'll provide a sample load script that runs curl/post to the endpoint with representative payloads.
[03:41] Omar: Are you able to run the bench from within our VPC so network path mirrors production?
[03:45] Samir: Yes, if you set up either peering or PrivateLink we can spin up a Redwood-managed runner in your VPC or you can run the script from your side. For strict egress, it's better for you to run the client inside your account and we run the server side on reserved infra.
[03:58] Lena: We'll likely run the client internally. We'll also want to baseline latency to your platform from our VPC.
[04:04] Maya: Great. Timeline proposal: get network details and security questions answered by 2028-06-17, Redwood shares benchmark plan 2028-06-20, pilot window 2028-06-24 to 2028-06-28, analyze results and decision meeting by 2028-07-02. That fits a 2-week pilot.
[04:20] Priya: That timeline seems ok if we can get the security docs quickly.
[04:24] Maya: We'll send SOC2 + SOC3 excerpts and the PrivateLink peering runbook by Friday.
[04:29] Samir: One more technical detail — NAT/Egress: if your subnet blocks all outbound, and you go with VPC peering, note that peering relies on route tables; you must ensure peering routes are propagated and not blocked by NACLs. With PrivateLink the egress stays inside AWS backbone.
[04:44] Lena: Good point. Our network team is conservative; PrivateLink may be easier for them. Any cost differences to note?
[04:50] Samir: PrivateLink has per-GB and endpoint-hour charges on your side but avoids touching route tables. Peering has no per-GB peering charge on AWS, but cross-account transfer costs could apply depending on traffic path and AZs. We'll include approximate cost pointers in the runbook.
[05:02] Omar: For acceptance tests: 1) run 30 QPS stable for 10 minutes with p95 <= 120ms on typical workload; 2) worst-case 512 token p95 <= 250ms; 3) logs delivered and no payload persistence; 4) a sample set of prompts must return semantically coherent outputs matching baseline accuracy.
[05:20] Maya: We'll document those as acceptance tests. Any other blockers?
[05:24] Priya: Confirm that keys or creds for metrics forwarding won't be stored beyond the pilot, and that role access is limited.
[05:30] Samir: We'll use cross-account role with least privilege and provide steps to rotate/tear down after pilot.
[05:35] Lena: Ok. We'll circulate VPC details internally and expect to have them by Monday.
[05:40] Maya: Perfect. Quick recap of next steps: Maya send docs by 6/18, Samir benchmark by 6/20, Everwell share network details by 6/17, schedule pilot week of 6/24.
[05:50] Omar: Thanks, sounds good.
[05:52] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in CRM with the action items.
[05:55] Call ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and minor word substitutions (e.g., "NHS? endpoint" instead of "VPC endpoint" in auto-transcript).
